headline: Domestic Chinese semiconductor supply chain is being forced to innovate and reaching 30-40% self-reliance; investable opportunities emerging in chips and equipment
reasoning: Over five to six years of US export restrictions, China has built out a domestic semiconductor supply chain covering chips and equipment. While generally still behind Western equivalents, some segments are competitive and a few Chinese equipment makers even supply TSMC. China is now roughly 30-40% self-reliant on its semiconductor needs, up from near-zero a decade ago. This creates investment opportunities in Chinese chip designers competing with Nvidia and in equipment makers competing with Applied Materials and Lam Research.

A domestic supply chain for semiconductors is getting built for these chips... the Chinese are finding ways to actually make their own chips... they're getting their own stack in terms of the whole sort of semiconductor industry becoming more and more self-reliant... ten years ago they probably import most of it. Now they're probably self reliant on, you know, 30 or 40% of, of the, of the needs.

Both sides are in a stalemate, with the US restricting advanced semiconductor exports to China and China holding the rare earth card.
